To illustrate workflow with Stan and Julia, let's consider a situation in which salaries are based, imperfectly, on a number of latent talents. Additionally, let us assume that there are some underlying biases on the basis of protected characteristics, like sex and race/ethnicity. Let us see how sensitive our regression methods are to discovering these biases.

We load a number of Julia packages to process tabular data, work with random distributions, etc.

```{julia}
# packages
using DataFrames
using DataFramesMeta
using Distributions
# built-in packages
using Random
```

## Generating synthetic data

### Generating parameters

We use $N$ for the number of individuals with salaries and $G$ for the number of groups (think: departments or job classes).

```{julia}
N = 1000
G = 20
```

We generate the sizes of each department by using a categorical distribution where the probabilities are normalized from draws from the uniform distribution. For each $g = 1, \ldots, G$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_g &\sim \text{Uniform}(0, 1) \\
p_g &= \frac{P_g}{\sum\limits_h P_h}.
\end{aligned}
$$

```{julia}
Random.seed!(20240721)

P_group = rand(Uniform(), G)
p_group = P_group ./ sum(P_group)
```

Without loss of generality, we sort these by renumbering the groups.

```{julia}
p_group = reverse(sort(p_group))
```

It's time to start considering the group parameters as a data frame.

```{julia}
group_params = DataFrame(id_group = 1:G, p_group = p_group)
```

We can add more parameters as necessary. Since we imagine salary to be log-normally distributed, with a distribution that may differ by group, we set mu and sigma, through the CV (coefficient of variation), for each group.

```{julia}
transform!(group_params, [] => (() -> rand(Uniform(10.3, 12.8), G)) => :μ)
transform!(group_params, [] => (() -> rand(Uniform(0.03, 0.15), G)) => :cv)
transform!(group_params, [:μ, :cv] => ((μ, cv) -> μ .* cv) => :σ)
```

We can also calculate the exponentiated mean, median, mode, standard deviation, etc.

```{julia}
transform!(group_params, [:μ] => ((μ) -> exp.(μ)) => :median)
transform!(group_params, [:μ, :σ] => ((μ, σ) -> exp.(μ .- σ.^2)) => :mode)
transform!(group_params, [:μ, :σ] => ((μ, σ) -> exp.(μ .+ 0.5.*σ.^2)) => :mean)
transform!(group_params, [:mean, :σ] => ((mean, σ) -> mean .* sqrt.(exp.(σ.^2) .- 1)) => :std_dev)
transform!(group_params, [:σ] => ((σ) -> (exp.(σ.^2) .+ 2) .* sqrt.(exp.(σ.^2) .- 1)) => :skewness)
transform!(group_params, [:σ] => ((σ) -> (exp.(4 .* σ.^2) .+ 2 .* exp.(3 .* σ.^2) .+ 3 .* exp.(2 .* σ.^2) .- 6)) => :excess_kurtosis)
```

We can then assign all $N$ individuals to groups, similarly renumbering them to order by group.

```{julia}
group = rand(Categorical(p_group), N)
group = sort(group)
```

We begin to assemble this into a data frame.

```{julia}
individual_parameters = DataFrame(id_group = group)
```

How many latent skills should we include? Let's call that number $S$.

```{julia}
S = 5
skill_names = [Symbol("skill_$i") for i in 1:S]
```

```{julia}
skills_data = rand(Normal(), (N, S))
```

```{julia}
insertcols!(individual_parameters, (skill_names .=> eachcol(skills_data))...)
```

### Cleaning up: Assembling private parameters into a function

Scripts are nice for testing things, but we should refactor our code into a function so that we can run many possible scenarios. Here's the basic architecture:

```{mermaid}
---
title: Data flow
---
flowchart LR
    n_skills --> universal_parameters
    n_groups --> group_parameters
    universal_parameters --> group_parameters
    group_parameters --> private_parameters
    n_people --> private_parameters
    private_parameters --> public_parameters
    n_observable_skills --> public_parameters
    skill_noise --> public_parameters
    salary_noise --> public_parameters
```

```{julia}
# Returns parameters governing all observation
function universal_parameters(n_skills)
    universal_params = DataFrame(
        μ_lo = 10.3,
        μ_hi = 12.8,
        cv_lo = 0.03,
        cv_hi = 0.15,
        n_skills = n_skills
    )
    β_names = [Symbol("β_skill_$i") for i in 1:n_skills]
    β = rand(Normal(), (1, n_skills))
    insertcols!(universal_params, (β_names .=> eachcol(β))...)
end

# Returns group parameters for n_groups, sorted in reverse by frequency
function group_parameters(n_groups, universal_params)
    relative_group_frequency = rand(Uniform(), n_groups)
    # Normalize to get probabilities
    group_probabilities = relative_group_frequency ./ sum(relative_group_frequency)
    group_probabilities = reverse(sort(group_probabilities))
    group_params = DataFrame(id_group = 1:n_groups, p_group = group_probabilities)
    group_params = crossjoin(group_params, universal_params)
    transform!(group_params, [:μ_lo, :μ_hi] => ((μ_lo, μ_hi) -> rand.(Uniform.(μ_lo, μ_hi), 1) |> Iterators.flatten |> collect) => :μ)
    transform!(group_params, [:cv_lo, :cv_hi] => ((cv_lo, cv_hi) -> rand.(Uniform.(cv_lo, cv_hi), 1) |> Iterators.flatten |> collect) => :cv)
    transform!(group_params, [:μ, :cv] => ((μ, cv) -> μ .* cv) => :σ)
    transform!(group_params, [:μ] => ((μ) -> exp.(μ)) => :median)
    transform!(group_params, [:μ, :σ] => ((μ, σ) -> exp.(μ .- σ.^2)) => :mode)
    transform!(group_params, [:μ, :σ] => ((μ, σ) -> exp.(μ .+ 0.5.*σ.^2)) => :mean)
    transform!(group_params, [:mean, :σ] => ((mean, σ) -> mean .* sqrt.(exp.(σ.^2) .- 1)) => :std_dev)
    transform!(group_params, [:σ] => ((σ) -> (exp.(σ.^2) .+ 2) .* sqrt.(exp.(σ.^2) .- 1)) => :skewness)
    transform!(group_params, [:σ] => ((σ) -> (exp.(4 .* σ.^2) .+ 2 .* exp.(3 .* σ.^2) .+ 3 .* exp.(2 .* σ.^2) .- 6)) => :excess_kurtosis)
    group_params
end

# Generates groups from parameters and number of people
function groups(group_params, n_people)
    group = rand(Categorical(group_params[!, :p_group]), n_people)
    group = sort(group)
    DataFrame(id_group = group)
end

function skills(n_skills, n_people)
    skill_names = [Symbol("skill_$i") for i in 1:n_skills]
    skill_data = rand(Normal(), (n_people, n_skills))
    DataFrame(skill_data, skill_names)
end

function private_parameters(n_people, group_params)
    n_skills = min(group_params(:, :n_skills))
    private_params = groups(group_params, n_people)
    DataFrames.hcat!(private_params, skills(n_skills, n_people))
    private_params = innerjoin(private_params, group_params, on=:id_group)
    
    μ = private_params[:, :μ]
    β_skill = Matrix(select(private_params, Cols(x -> startswith(x, "β_skill_"))))'[:, 1]
    X_skill = Matrix(select(private_params, Cols(x -> startswith(x, "skill_"))))
    expected_log_salary = μ + X_skill * β_skill
    σ = private_params[:, :σ]
    log_salary = [rand(Normal(μ1, σ1)) for (μ1 , σ1) in zip(expected_log_salary, σ)]

    insertcols!(private_params, :expected_log_salary => expected_log_salary, :log_salary => log_salary)
    private_params
end

function public_parameters(private_params, n_observable_skills, skill_noise, salary_noise)
    n_people = nrow(private_params)
    observable_skill_names = [Symbol("skill_$i") for i in 1:n_observable_skills]
    public_params = select(private_params, :id_group, observable_skill_names..., :log_salary)
    # add noise
    transform!(public_params, [:log_salary] => (s -> s .+ rand(Normal(0, salary_noise), n_people)) => :log_salary)
    transform!(public_params, observable_skill_names .=> Ref(s -> s .+ rand(Normal(0, skill_noise), n_people)) .=> observable_skill_names)
    public_params
end

S = 5
universal_params = universal_parameters(S)
G = 3
group_params = group_parameters(G, universal_params)
N = 10
private_params = private_parameters(N, S, group_params)
s = 3
public_params = public_parameters(private_params, s, 0.1, 0)
```

Here, we have imagined $\forall i\in\lbrace 1\ldots N\rbrace$, where $g(i)$ is the group of the $i\text{th}$ person. 

$$
\log \text{Salary}_{i} \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{g(i)} + \sum\limits_{j=1}^{S} \text{Skill}_{ij}\beta_j, \sigma^2_{g(i)})
$$

Only some of the skills ($s$ of $S$) are measured, and these with Gaussian noise `skill_noise`. Optionally, one can add in `salary_noise`, but we give the HR team the benefit of the doubt in assigning salary.



```{julia}
insertcols!(public_skill_data)
```





```{stan}
data {
    // Number of observations
    int<lower=0> N;
    // Number of latent explanatory features
    int<lower=0> P;
    // Number of groups
    int<lower=0> G;
    // Size of fuzz
    real<lower=0> fuzz;
}
generated quantities {
    vector[N] y;
    matrix[N, P] Latent;
    matrix[N, P] X;
    real beta_0;
    vector[P] beta_latent;
    beta_0 = normal_rng(10, 1);
    for (p in 1:P) {
        beta_latent[p] = normal_rng(0, 1);
    }
    for (n in 1:N) {
        for (p in 1:P) {
            Latent[n, p] = normal_rng(0, 1);
            X[n, p] = Latent[n, p] + normal_rng(0, fuzz);
        }
        y[n] = normal_rng(beta_0 + Latent[n]*beta_latent, 1);
    }
}
```
